subject: Finalizing Vectra multi-year prepay and billing cadence
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@vectra.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@vectra.ai
Date: 2026-09-30T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Options for 3yr prepay + split invoicing for FY reporting

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood. Procurement and finance asked me to get clarity on a couple of things so we can close the PO this quarter:

- We want a 3-year prepay commitment but need invoices aligned to our fiscal years (we run Oct–Sep). Can Redwood split the prepay so we receive an invoice per customer fiscal year (i.e., invoice now for FY27 portion, then FY28, FY29)?
- From a revenue recognition perspective, our auditors require a short statement on how prepay will be recognized; can you confirm how Redwood treats a multi-year prepay for ASC 606 purposes? Will Redwood issue an invoice for each year with a note that revenue is deferred and recognized over the service period?
- Any recommendations on ramping credits across years (we expect usage to be heavier in year 1). Is there an option to frontload credits while keeping invoices split by year?

If you can share a sample term-sheet or billing language we can attach to the PO, that would speed things up.

Appreciate the help — looping in our procurement lead Daniel.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Head of Platform Partnerships
Vectra AI

(attachment: n/a)

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Elena Rossi <elena@vectra.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-30T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Options for 3yr prepay + split invoicing for FY reporting

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, details below: yes, we can support split invoicing by customer fiscal year; yes, we will provide written language about revenue deferral/recognition; and yes, we can frontload credits to year 1 while keeping invoices split. I attached a first-pass proposal and a term-sheet stub you can circulate.

High-level commercial structure we recommend for your case:
- Commitment: 36 months prepaid.
- List price commitment: $1,200,000 ARR equivalent (billed as a 3-year prepay).
- Commercial discount: 20% term discount applied to committed spend (annualized view).
- Invoicing cadence (customer preference): split by fiscal year — we can issue three invoices mapped to your FY27/FY28/FY29 amounts. Proposed split (negotiable): FY27: 50% of total prepay, FY28: 30%, FY29: 20%. This frontloads cash for you to use credits in year 1 while keeping FY invoices aligned.

Revenue recognition note (summary):
- We will issue invoices per your requested cadences. For Redwood accounting: the invoices are recorded as deferred revenue and recognized ratably over the 36-month service period (consistent with ASC 606). We can provide one-sentence language for your auditors confirming deferral and the service period for the contract. Marcus (cc) can confirm the canonical wording we use.

Optional variant: if you prefer a more even split for your internal budgeting, we can do 40/30/30 instead — flexible.

Next steps I suggest:
1) You confirm which split you want (50/30/20 vs 40/30/30).
2) We send an updated term-sheet with explicit invoicing and rev-rec language for your PO/auditors.
3) Procurement provides PO and preferred billing address/tax details.

Attached: proposal_vectra_redwood_v1.pdf (proposal stub)

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min call if Daniel wants to walk through the numbers.

—
Tessa Morgan
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Email: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, Elena Rossi <elena@vectra.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Options for 3yr prepay + split invoicing for FY reporting

Tessa/Elena — quick finance perspective to make sure auditors have what they need.

1) Invoicing model and AR: Redwood can issue three separate invoices aligned to Vectra's fiscal years. Each invoice will be recorded as cash/AR on our books and credited to a deferred revenue liability (contract liability).

2) Revenue recognition policy (standard wording we can provide): "Payments received in advance of the performance obligation are recorded as deferred revenue and recognized on a straight-line basis over the contract term (36 months) unless there is a separate, distinct performance obligation identified in the contract. Redwood Inference will provide an invoice and confirmation of the service period for each invoice to support customer audit requests."

3) Accounting entries (illustrative):
- On invoice receipt: Dr Cash / Cr Deferred Revenue (contract liability).
- Monthly recognition: Dr Deferred Revenue / Cr Revenue (recognized ratably over months in scope).

4) Tax & billing ops: please ensure we have the correct billing entity and tax jurisdiction on the PO (we will need VAT/GST instructions if applicable). Also confirm whether Vectra requires an invoice with line-level allocations to model credits vs. support (we can provide a consolidated invoice or a line-item breakdown).

5) On frontloading credits: technically we can credit more usage up-front (i.e., allocate more of the prepaid value as a credit coupon in year 1). From an accounting POV the total deferred revenue still equals the prepay; the credits change only how customers consume the value. If Vectra needs an explicit schedule of credit allocations for internal finance, we can include it as an annex to the term-sheet.

If you want the exact rev-rec paragraph for the contract, I can drop a finalized sentence for legal/auditor sign-off.

—Marcus Lin
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
(marcus_lin@redwood.ai)

Thanks Tessa/Marcus — this is very helpful. A few clarifying points from procurement/finance:

- We’ll take the 50/30/20 split (FY27/FY28/FY29).
- For audit purposes, can Redwood add the rev-rec sentence Marcus provided into the term-sheet or the master services agreement as a short clause? Our auditors want the confirmation in writing tied to the contract.
- Regarding credits: we will accept the credits frontloaded into year 1 but ask that the term-sheet includes a credit allocation table showing the dollar value available per year (so our finance team can map cost centers).
- PO timing: procurement will issue a PO once we have the updated term-sheet and a DocuSign envelope for an authorized signature.

If you can send an updated term-sheet with the clause and the credit allocation table today, we can push the PO and sign-off this week.

Best,
Elena
